description:
Least-privilege capability for the SEPARATE 'Driftstack Simulator' macOS app build (tauri.simulator.conf.json). The first config-created window keeps label `main`; Rust consumes the complete owner-only single-use handoff file selected by the non-secret `--ds-label` argument before applying its internal URL. This capability targets `main`; dynamically-created per-session windows inherit the same explicit set. The separate-app build sets app.security.capabilities=["simulator-app"] in its config, which OVERRIDES the default auto-inclusion of capabilities/*.json — so the separate app gets ONLY this set and NEVER the broad `default` capability (audit 1.8 least-privilege). Deliberately EXCLUDES shell / updater / process / deep-link / create-webview-window — none are reachable from the simulator entry (main.tsx ?window=simulator → RecordingsProvider + SimulatorWindow). The grants below are exactly what the simulator window + the libs it imports actually use:
  • window mutation: start-dragging (frame drag), close + destroy (X button + onCloseRequested teardown), minimize, set-size (rotate/resize), set-always-on-top (pin), set-focus.
  • core:window:default — read-only window queries.
  • core:webview:default — getCurrentWebviewWindow + onCloseRequested.
  • core:event:default — listen('ds-session') relaunch re-point.
  • core / app / resources — baseline IPC.
  • store:default — lib/settings.ts LazyStore get/set/save in loadSettings().
  • fs (read/write text, mkdir, remove, exists, read-dir) scoped to $APPDATA/recordings/** — RecordingsProvider.loadIndex() runs on mount; the Record pill persists frames there.
  • fs:scope $DOWNLOAD/** + fs:allow-write-file — the snapshot button writes a PNG to Downloads.
App-defined commands (secret_load/secret_save/secret_delete for OS credential-store persistence, set_dock_tile/reset_dock_tile for the dynamic macOS Dock icon — the proxy country flag captioned with the profile name) need NO ACL entry in Tauri v2 — locally-registered commands are always callable; only plugin/core permissions are listed here.
